g.text: WLD 205 DAY 7 — INSTRUCTOR KEY / DELIVERY GUIDE
Math Recovery III: Tolerances + Accept/Reject Reasoning
0–8 MIN — TOLERANCE RETRIEVAL
Use the three Tolerance Cards. Students identify nominal, variation, lower limit, upper limit, and units.
Live Questions 1–3. Correct the limit calculation before moving into accept/reject decisions.
Cue: “Do not judge the actual until both limits are written.”
8–20 MIN — DECISION MODEL
NOMINAL → LIMITS → ACTUAL → DECISION
Model one accepted case and one rejected case. Keep units through every step.
Accepted example: 2.000 ± 0.030 in, actual 2.025 in → inside 1.970–2.030.
Rejected example: 2.000 ± 0.030 in, actual 2.036 in → above 2.030 upper limit.
Never round an out-of-tolerance value into acceptance.
20–40 MIN — TOLERANCE SET A
Students complete six decimal accept/reject cases. The fractional limit problem was handled in the retrieval cards.
Q4: 2.025 → ACCEPT. Q5: 2.036 → REJECT.
Q6: 6.490 → ACCEPT. Q7: 6.518 → REJECT.
Q8: 1.481 → ACCEPT. Q9: 1.477 → REJECT.
Require written lower/upper limits and units before students select the live answer.
If an error occurs, identify whether the gap is calculation, comparison, or decision rather than reteaching all six.
40–54 MIN — MEASUREMENT RECORD + CORRECTIVE NOTE
B: 7.984 for 8.000 ± 0.010 → REJECT (7.990–8.010). This is the out-of-tolerance record.
Model note: “Dimension B measured 7.984 in, below lower limit 7.990 in; hold for correction/recheck per instructor/project procedure.”
Live Questions 10–11. Preserve the original measurement. Do not rewrite the requirement to fit the part.
54–60 MIN — 4-ITEM INDEPENDENT CHECK
No coaching. Q12: 3.242 → ACCEPT. Q13: 5.020 → REJECT. Q14: 1.871 → ACCEPT.
Q15 checks the complete decision chain: NOMINAL → LIMITS → ACTUAL → DECISION.
Record only the unresolved domain: Calculate Limits • Compare Actual • Accept/Reject • Document/Recheck.
Focused retry: model one parallel case, then require one independent recheck. Do not repeat demonstrated domains.

svg.text: Real job acceptance and corrective action remain controlled by the approved print/tolerance source and applicable instructor/project procedure.
